verdict.rationale: Checkout.com Issuing documents single- or multi-use virtual cards with granular limits on transaction amounts, blocked industries and card expiry dates, plus custom accept/reject authorization rules. That covers the mechanics of a scoped spend card. However, nothing in the evidence documents issuing cards to AI agents by name, and merchant-level locks are shown only as industry blocking or self-built rules. Missing for 10: vendor-documented AI-agent card use case, explicit per-merchant locking, any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give an agent its own card — issue a scoped virtual card to an AI agent with merchant locks, amount caps, and expiry so autonomous purchases stay inside policy, a use the vendor documents by name

citations.quote: Our platform supports physical cards and single or multi-use virtual cards for online, offline, or in-app payments.
Set granular limits like transaction amounts, blocked industries, and card expiry dates.
Automate transaction outcomes with accept or reject logic based on your own rules.
